title: MZR Archive Census — what the archives actually hold

cards.heading: What do the archives actually hold?
cards.body: A pre-registered census of catalogues carrying gas-phase metallicity, stellar mass and redshift together. NebulaMind Lab.

cards.heading: The spread this work is about
cards.body: 304 published metallicity values, coloured by method. The vertical spread at fixed redshift is the problem this census exists to measure.

cards.heading: The method is the point
cards.body: Two enumeration channels over VizieR: semantic UCD tags, and column names in every case variant. The contract was frozen and hash-pinned before a single row was counted.
candidate tables carry all three axes, drawn from 178 before the modifier filter, with 21 dropped and each drop recorded.

cards.heading: Reach is not eligibility
cards.body: Of the candidates carrying all three axes, this many hold explicit gas-phase evidence.
of those candidates carry explicit gas-phase evidence in their own recorded descriptions.

cards.heading: The instrument was tested before it was trusted
cards.body: Seven recall members had to come back and three controls had to stay out. They did. The recall set was sha-pinned before the run and read from the pinned file, never retyped.

cards.heading: The rules are now frozen
cards.body: The eligibility contract was frozen after 7 gate rounds, with 12 decoys planted to catch rules that admit too much. Frozen before any table was judged, so it could not be bent to fit a result.

cards.heading: What the census does NOT establish
cards.body: Reach is not eligibility. The redshift tag is applied to the symbol Z, not the concept — stellar coordinates, gravitational redshifts and model grids all enter candidacy. Ruling them out is a separate, gated stage.

cards.heading: nebulamind.net
cards.body: Contract frozen before measurement. Every number read from a recorded artifact.
